name: Backside 50/50 Control
keyCorrections: If they turn to face you, you lost hip control, re-establish your grip on their far hip.
If you can't find the heel, you're too low on their leg, scoot up toward their hip.
If they kick free, your leg entanglement was too loose, tighten your 50/50 control.
description: Control the backside 50/50, a leg entanglement position behind the opponent's hip line that generates Heel Hook threats without requiring the full Saddle position.
shortInstruction: Behind the hip, inside leg control, manage their far leg, backside 50/50 is the Back Take of the Leg Lock world.
summary: Backside 50/50 is a leg entanglement position where you are positioned behind the opponent's hip line with both of your legs controlling one of their legs in a 50/50 configuration. The key advantage over the Saddle is that you are behind them, they cannot see your attacks and have limited escape options. From here, you can attack the Heel Hook, transition to the Saddle, or take the back.
whyItWorks: Being behind their hip line gives you a positional advantage, they cannot see your hands or leg positioning.
The 50/50 leg configuration gives you strong control of their far leg while your hands attack the near leg.
It transitions easily to Saddle or Back Take depending on their reaction.
Danaher principle: position before submission, backside 50/50 is the position; the Heel Hook is the submission.
commonMistakes: Losing control of their far leg, the far leg is their escape route.
Letting them turn and face you, once they face you, backside 50/50 becomes standard 50/50.
Focusing only on the Heel Hook and ignoring the Back Take, both must be threats.
Sitting too low on their leg, you need to be high on their thigh for control.
coachingCues: Behind the hip, you control the game.
Far leg is the key, control it or lose the position.
If they turn, take the back. If they stay, Heel Hook.
Stay high on the leg, ankle control gives you nothing.
safetySummary: The backside 50/50 position can apply rotational pressure to the knee, apply Heel Hooks slowly and carefully.
Do not cranking the Heel Hook from backside 50/50 without establishing clear control of their hip.
Establish tap protocols for all leg attacks before training.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Enter backside 50/50 (behind their hip, 50/50 leg position): control their far leg → attack Heel Hook or transition.

decisionTree.action: They stay facing away → Heel Hook finish.
They turn toward you → transition to Saddle or Back Take.
Backside 50/50 is the entry; Saddle and Back Take are the destinations.

moneyDetails: Your position should be high on their thigh, not low on their calf, high position gives you hip control.
Control their far leg by trapping it between your legs or grabbing their ankle with your free hand.
Keep your chest close to their hip, the closer you are, the less they can move.
When they turn toward you, follow their hips and enter Saddle or take the back, don't stay in 50/50.
nextStep: After backside 50/50, learn the Saddle control and Heel Hook finishes.
fixItFast: They keep turning? Follow their hip and take the back.
Can't find the heel? Scoot higher on their leg.
They kick free? Re-establish the 50/50 entanglement tighter.
